correctness.rationale: For even q≥2 with δ=q^-2, r=(q+1)/q, H=sqrt(1+δ²/4), L=(q+1)δ, periodic φ describes Liao–Wang geodesic tile T_q between y=φ(x) and y=rφ(x/r). The reflection axis x0=L/2 passes through a lower arc crest H and upper concave corner of height r. Axis balls obey ρ≤min(log(y/H),log(r/y)), with equality only at y0=sqrt(rH); the hyperbolic ball of radius ρ0=.5log(r/H) has Euclidean horizontal half-width (r-H)/2, fits [0,L]×[H,r]⊂T_q, proving sharp axis constraint. The ball touches only lower smooth arc at A and upper strict corner B. On moving center horizontally by t, distance to the lower supporting geodesic is arsinh((t²+y0²-H²)/(2Hy0))>ρ0, while the locally nearest upper corner has cosh distance coshρ0+t²/(2r y0)>coshρ0; one-sided upper distance derivatives remain strict. Compact separation from all other boundary parts completes a strict improvement for small nonzero t. Reflection then yields distinct maximizing centers. No exact unrestricted inradius or odd-q result is claimed.
